root_causes: Inefficient high-level planning leading to early Rearrange commands while all objects were still far away on table_30, causing multi-step, long-distance transports and associated penalties.
Suboptimal role allocation between the two agents, with one agent frequently executing Wait[None] instead of parallelizing retrieval and placement to minimize idle time.

Redundant or prolonged execution of the same Rearrange subgoals (e.g., repeated Rearrange calls for objects already en route or nearly placed), increasing step count and negative reward without improving task progress.

Lack of explicit termination of grasp/transport once placement is achieved, resulting in agents still holding objects after all propositions were satisfied, which may reflect incomplete post-task cleanup behavior.
improvement_suggestions: Plan retrieval and placement in phases: first navigate both agents to the table_30 area, collect objects efficiently, then move to bench_51, to reduce long-distance per-object Rearrange penalties.
Exploit parallelism more aggressively by assigning distinct objects or subtasks to each agent, avoiding extended Wait[None] while the other agent is active.
Introduce checks before issuing Rearrange actions to avoid re-commanding moves for objects already correctly placed or already in transit to the target.

Add explicit post-placement policies (e.g., drop/ungasp once an object is confirmed on the target receptacle) to avoid agents unnecessarily holding objects after success and to reduce potential extra steps.
Use cost-aware planning (e.g., penalize long navigation + multiple replans) to prefer action sequences with shorter paths and fewer redundant replan windows.
overall_assessment: The task was completed successfully with all three items placed on the bench, but the trajectory incurred unnecessary negative reward due to inefficient planning, redundant rearrange commands, and underutilization of the second agent. Overall execution was correct but only moderately efficient.
task_instruction: Put the mug, squeezer, and toy food on the bench in the entryway.
